headline: COP31 climate talks deadlocked over fossil fuels
pages: UN climate talks at COP31 in Turkey are deadlocked after running more than 24 hours past their scheduled end. Delegates have been unable to agree on a new global climate deal. The main sticking point is whether the text should mention moving away from fossil fuels. A group led by France and Panama objected on Friday to a draft that left out any reference to cutting demand for oil, gas and coal, after producers led by Saudi Arabia pushed to remove it. A second dispute involves a push from the Africa Group for firm commitments on more adaptation money, which the EU has said it will not support.

Some negotiators due to fly home Sunday have moved their flights to Monday, a sign that no deal is close. If too many countries leave, the meeting could lack the number needed to pass an agreement and would be suspended, which has happened only once before in 24 years of these talks. Why it matters: the outcome will set the tone for global climate policy. Source: BBC.
